newsitem.title: LATVIA: IMF says Latvia GDP could grow 5 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: IMF says Latvia GDP could grow 5 pct in 1997.

text.p: Latvia's International Monetray Fund (IMF) representative said the Baltic state's gross domestic product (GDP) could grow by five percent in 1997, the Latvian daily Diena reported on Monday.
"The IMF believes that the five-percent growth target (for 1997) set by the government is realistic and achievable," Dimitris Demekas said in an interview with the paper.
"To achieve that, however, Latvia should press on quickly as possible with the privatisation of large enterprises."
Demenkas said falling inflation and interest rates, an elastic labour market and a strong political commitment to reform were key factors driving the country's growth prospects.

"Not a single serious political party in Latvia supports a return to government control over production and business...It is important for the world to know that reform will continue even if the government were to change," he added.
The country's economy is expected to expand two percent this year.
GDP shrank 1.6 percent last year as a result of a banking crisis which sapped investor confidence and stalled recovery.
Five years after quitting the Soviet Union, most of the country's GDP is attributed to the private sector and most small- and medium-sized enterprises have been privatised.
But many large enterprises, such as the Latvian Shipping cpmpany, remain in the hands of the state. But the government has pledged to privatise most of them within the next two years.
